verbs.name: render.preview
verbs.description: Fast low-res render of a window starting at at_ms (default 5000ms) for quick agent/human review, OR (draft:true) the incremental whole-timeline draft preview: the export's frames at draft size (the project's aspect inside 960x540) — every output frame shows the same source frame as render.final at the same index, with the same length, speed, reversed clips, captions and overlays. It is made of pieces cut at the base track's clip boundaries; after an edit only the pieces whose content changed are remade and the rest are reused (a piece moved by a whole number of frames is reused). DERIVED state (cache under proxies/preview-cache/), never an op, never a receipt input — receipts stay render.final.

at_ms.description: Window start (window mode only; REQUIRED unless draft:true). Ignored when draft:true (the preview is the whole timeline).

duration_ms.description: Window length (window mode only). Ignored when draft:true.

draft.description: Incremental whole-timeline draft preview (the export's frames at draft size, piece cache). When true, at_ms/duration_ms are ignored and the result names which pieces were remade vs reused.

verbs.result: {path, mime} window mode; {path, mime, draft:true, segments_rendered, segments_reused, rendered[], reused[], duration_ms} draft mode

verbs.name: render.frame
verbs.description: Compose one frame at at_ms — the agent's eyes / the human scrub frame without a full render. Fast scrub path: by default serves a fast proxy-seek frame (no captions/overlay) scaled to height h; compose:true forces the EXACT composed frame (captions + overlays at project geometry — the agent's verify eyes). The frame shown at at_ms is the frame the export has on screen then: output frame floor(at_ms*fps/1000) with half a millisecond of tolerance (a playhead put on a frame reads its rounded start); the fast path shows the same source frame from the proxy, and falls back to the composed frame where a clip converts its frame rate. Preview frames are bounded to 4K UHD resource limits; use export.frame for an explicit full-resolution still. returns {path, mime}; inline:true adds base64. Raw bytes also at GET /api/frame?at_ms=[&h=][&compose=1] (X-Cut-Frame-Fast header reports the path used).

h.description: scale the frame to this height in px (preview size, up to 2160). Default 540 (the proxy height). Width and total pixels are bounded to a 4K UHD preview budget; use export.frame for an explicit full-resolution still.

compose.description: force the EXACT composed frame (captions + overlays, project geometry) instead of the fast proxy scrub frame. The agent's verify eyes.

verbs.result: {path, mime, at_ms, width, height, fast, base64?}

verbs.name: render.compare
verbs.description: Read-only Preview comparison: render the exact composed durable-head frame and the exact timeline state immediately before the latest timeline-mutating operation at one playhead position. Trailing metadata remains part of the current head but never becomes a deceptive identical Before frame. The caller supplies the observed current revision; stale heads, changed sequence/geometry/cadence, and missing prior visible composition refuse instead of guessing or moving the project's undo state. The two JPEGs are base64 in one bounded response; no project operation, undo, export, or persisted comparison file is created.

at_ms.description: Exact timeline frame to compare in both revisions.

revision.description: The durable project revision observed by the Preview before it opens comparison. A changed head refuses so before/current frames cannot be mixed.

h.description: Height of each exact comparison frame in px. Capped at 1080 because one request renders a bounded pair.

verbs.name: render.storyboard
verbs.description: Contact sheet: `count` evenly-spaced frames of the composed timeline tiled into a grid image — the agent/judge's see-the-whole-edit-at-a-glance view (one image instead of N frame fetches). Fast proxy-scrub frames by default; compose:true forces exact composed frames (captions/overlays). Single-frame extraction failures are replaced with black placeholder tiles and reported in frame_warnings. Written to the engine-owned frames/ dir.

count.description: Number of frames in the contact sheet (default 12).

compose.description: Force exact composed frames (captions/overlays) instead of fast proxy-scrub.

verbs.result: {path, mime, count, grid:[cols,rows], frame_height, duration_ms, fallback_frames, frame_warnings:[{index,at_ms,code,message,cause}]} (+base64 when inline)

verbs.name: render.reframe
verbs.description: Subject-aware auto-reframe (job, returns {reframe_id, job_id}). Renders the timeline to a temp at project geometry (the finished edit), runs the `subject` perception instrument (local CV: detect+track+saliency -> a normalized, aspect-independent subject track), then a subject-tracked moving-crop POST-PASS to the target aspect. The HONEST replacement for render.final{aspect,fit:cover} (which is a naive STATIC centre-crop that ignores the subject): this FOLLOWS the subject with a smoothed pan, original render untouched. Output default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4; an explicit fenced path must also end in .mp4. The receipt records subject-in-frame %, the device it analyzed on, and that reframe is a LOSSY crop (not a lossless conversion).

aspect.description: Target aspect ratio W:H with small integers, e.g. 9:16 (vertical), 1:1 (square), 4:5 (portrait), 16:9. Output dimensions are normalized to a 1080-px base, rounded even.

preset.description: Reframe preset: which subject classes to follow + the crop zoom/motion limits. talking_head (person, gentle), sports (person+vehicles, faster motion, less zoom), pets (dog/cat/person), cars (vehicles), general (all classes).

path.description: Optional explicit .mp4 output path (FENCED, canonicalized, no traversal/symlinks, project-or-outputs-dir only). Default <project>/exports/<reframe_id>.mp4.

direction.description: DIRECTOR brief from the foundation model: a per-scene framing decision that OVERRIDES the CV ranker for those scenes. Get the scenes + candidate subjects from render.direct's contact sheet, then map scene index -> the chosen candidate. Shape: {"<scene_idx>": {"cx": <0..1>}} to follow the subject at that normalized x (read each candidate's cx from the contact-sheet JSON), or {"<scene_idx>": {"mode": "widen"}} to hold a centered wide frame. Scenes you omit fall back to the CV ranker. The receipt records which scenes the director decided.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason for this reframe (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {reframe_id, job_id, aspect} — the output path + honesty receipt (subject_in_frame_pct, analyzed_on device, directed_scenes, reframe-is-lossy note) arrive in the job result; the receipt also carries encode:{encoder, hardware_requested:false, hardware_used:false} because the crop pass always encodes in software; render_done event on completion

verbs.name: render.direct
verbs.description: DIRECTOR pass for subject-aware reframe (job): renders the finished edit to a temp and builds a SPARSE per-scene CONTACT SHEET — one annotated keyframe per scene with the candidate subjects labeled A/B/C left->right — for a foundation model to direct the whole clip in one look. The local CV finds and tracks subjects; the model decides which subject each shot is about. Flow: call render.direct -> read the returned contact_sheet image + scenes[].candidates -> decide per scene -> call render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}}. Omitting the director falls back to the pure CV ranker.

preset.description: Which subject classes to consider as candidates (same set as render.reframe's preset). talking_head = person; sports = person+vehicles; pets = dog/cat/person; cars = vehicles; general = all.

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, direct_id} — the job result carries {contact_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, candidates:[{label, cls, cx, cy, box, has_face}]}]}; feed your per-scene pick into render.reframe{direction}

verbs.name: render.qc
verbs.description: DIRECTOR QC pass (job): REVIEW a reframed OUTPUT and decide what to fix. Resolves the actual render.reframe output from receipts/<reframe_id>.json output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Samples one keyframe per scene of the finished reframe and tiles them into a review sheet WITH cheap CV composition hints per scene — subject_present, face_present, face centering (off_center = |cx-0.5|), headroom (face-top y; a head clipped at the top), and a `needs_review` flag. A foundation model reads the qc_sheet image and for any bad scene re-issue render.reframe{aspect, direction:{<scene>:{cx}|{mode:'widen'}}} with a correction. Closes the director loop: direct -> reframe -> qc -> reframe.

reframe_id.description: The reframe output to review — the reframe_id returned by render.reframe. The actual output is resolved from the reframe receipt output_path, with legacy fallback to exports/<reframe_id>.mp4. Fenced: a bare id, no path separators.

preset.description: Candidate class set for the QC detector (same set as render.reframe's preset).

rationale.description: Optional human-readable reason (recorded for the operation history; does not affect the output).

verbs.result: {job_id, reframe_id} — the job result carries {qc_sheet (image path to read), scene_count, review_count, scenes:[{scene, t_ms, subject_present, face_present, face_cx, off_center, headroom, needs_review, issues}]}; re-issue render.reframe{direction} to fix flagged scenes

verbs.name: render.final
verbs.description: An older project with an odd frame size (e.g. 641x361) is refused up front with code odd_project_size when the render is at the project size (no aspect/width/height/match_source): video needs even sides; suggested_action is the exact project.format call (e.g. {"width":640,"height":360}). The same refusal applies to render.queue entries, render.direct, render.reframe, render.preview, export.range, export.gif and autopilot.run. Full render (job, returns {job_id}). A software render (hardware:off) repeats byte for byte on the same machine with the same encoder thread count; a hardware encoder, or a thread count adapted to free memory, can change the bytes. Default path: the export folder set with project.set_output_dir, else <project>/exports/<render_id>.<ext>; an explicit FENCED path must match the chosen container: .mp4 for h264/hevc/av1, .webm for vp9, or .mov for prores. On completion AUTO-runs the output-only RenderChecks battery → RenderReceipt; receipt_ready is always emitted after render_done. The async job result reports verified plus verification_status complete|unmeasured. Optional post-render instrumentation failures preserve verification_error, mark affected receipt rows details.status=unmeasured/details.measured=false with a plain details.reason ("not measured, because ...", also in result.verification_reason, with the next step in suggested_action), and never create content fix_actions. When the cause is a missing captions runtime (no Python of Cut's own yet), the reason is "captions and transcription are not installed" and the action is Install captions or system.setup_perception; the render itself is fine: the job finishes plainly done, result.pass is null (no verdict) and result.setup_needed names the missing piece and system.setup_perception. A timeline with an overlay track that is longer than one adaptive window (2 to 60 s, shorter at higher resolution and with more overlays), or any timeline longer than 10 minutes, or one with more than 4 GB of reversed video, renders in windows that are joined afterwards, so peak memory stays bounded regardless of duration; the result has exactly the frame count of a whole-graph render and every output frame shows the same source frame (each clip gets exactly round(out*fps) - round(in*fps) frames, and a clip whose source ends early holds its last frame); only the bytes differ, because the parts are encoded separately. A render whose ffmpeg writes nothing and does almost no work for 120 s fails with render_stalled, naming the timeline range, the clip and what to change. On Linux with a systemd user session each render's ffmpeg also runs in its own cgroup scope: MemoryHigh (75% of RAM by default) slows it and pushes memory to swap, and MemoryMax (RAM minus 1 GB) is a hard stop that ends only the render, which then fails with out_of_memory and the way out; macOS and Windows have no such limit. Tune segmentation/footprint via the SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_* env knobs (see SKILL.md Runtime knobs). An HDR source (HLG or PQ) is tone-mapped to SDR, which needs FFmpeg's zscale: without it render.final refuses up front with tool_missing naming the clip; encode.color in the plan, job result and receipt says what was done to each source. Before starting, a render whose project needs a filter no installed FFmpeg has (vid.stab for stabilized clips, libass for caption clips burned in, zimg for color management) is refused up front with code tool_missing, the feature, and how to get it or what to remove; the same check applies to render.queue, render.bundle, export.publish, export.range and autopilot.run.

preset.description: Quality tier (geometry/fps come from project settings): draft = fast review encode (x264 medium CRF 18, AAC 192k), standard = default (x264 slow CRF 20, AAC 192k), high = hero-asset tier (x264 slow CRF 17, AAC 256k). The receipt records the preset used. Within a non-h264 `format` it shifts that codec's rate knob.

format.description: Output FILE FORMAT (codec + container) — 'different file exports'. h264 = universal mp4 + AAC, the default golden combo (byte-identical to omitting format). hevc = H.265 mp4 (Apple hvc1 tag), ~30-50% smaller at equal quality. vp9 = VP9 + Opus.webm, royalty-free web-native. prores = ProRes 422.mov, the pro editing-handoff intermediate. av1 = AV1 mp4, the highest quality ceiling but SOFTWARE-slow here (libsvtav1) — use hardware tier for AV1 speed. The output extension follows the container; `preset` selects the quality tier within the codec.

hardware.description: Encoder tier. auto (default) = use the GPU/hardware encoder when the machine has one (NVENC/QSV/AMF/VideoToolbox) — much faster, and hardware AV1 is the quality ceiling. off = force the software encoder (reproducible on the same machine, maximum libx264 quality, no GPU). Only h264/hevc/av1 have a hardware tier (vp9/prores are software-only). The hardware encoder is PROBE-VERIFIED with a real test encode, so auto safely falls back to software when no working GPU encoder is present. The receipt's preset field records the encoder that actually ran (e.g. 'standard/hevc_nvenc'), and the receipt, the job result and a dry_run plan carry `encode` {encoder, hardware_requested, hardware_used, fallback_reason?, fallback_detail?}: when hardware was requested and software ran, fallback_reason says so in plain words (e.g. 'No usable hardware encoder was found, so this export used software encoding.') with what to do about it. A frame larger than the hardware encoder takes is named with that encoder's limit and, when another hardware codec takes it, the advice to choose it (e.g. 'The hardware encoder (h264_nvenc) accepts at most 4096x2160; this export is 7680x4320 ... Choose HEVC to encode this size in hardware (hevc_nvenc).'). When the hardware encoder fails DURING the render for a reason software does not share (out of video memory, the card's encode-session limit, a driver error, a frame size or pixel format the device refuses; NVENC, QSV, AMF and VideoToolbox messages are recognized), the render runs again with the software encoder of the same format and quality; the job shows that once as its progress message and encode.fallback_reason/fallback_detail say why (fallback_detail = the hardware encoder's own ffmpeg lines). When the GPU render path is asked for (environment SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_GPU=1), encode also carries pipeline ('gpu' or 'standard', the render path that ran) and, when the standard path ran, pipeline_reason in plain words (e.g. 'The GPU render path was asked for (SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_GPU), but a clip has ... reverse ..., which the GPU render path cannot draw, so this export used the standard render path.').

bitrate.description: Target VIDEO bitrate for rate-targeted publishing — e.g. '12M' (12 Mbps), '8000k', or a bare kbps number (50..500000 kbps). Omitted (DEFAULT) = quality-targeted CRF, byte-identical replay. Setting it switches the codec to a real bitrate target (needed to hit a platform spec — see export.publish). Works with the hardware tier (encoder-aware rewrite). ProRes ignores it (profile-fixed).

target_size_mb.description: Target output FILE SIZE in MB — 'fit under X' (Discord 25, email attach, WhatsApp). Computes the video bitrate that keeps the file UNDER the size (from the timeline duration, reserving audio, 90% headroom for VBR variance + container overhead) and renders VBR-under. Mutually exclusive with `bitrate`. Errors if the size is too small for the duration. ProRes ignores it.

rate_control.description: Rate control WHEN bitrate is set. vbr (default) = target AVERAGE, peaks capped ~1.45× for motion headroom; comes in UNDER on simple content (efficient — platform bitrates are ceilings). cbr = TRUE constant bitrate (x264 nal-hrd / x265 strict-cbr pad to the target) for strict-ingest platforms / live streaming. Errors if set without bitrate.

audio_bitrate.description: Target AUDIO bitrate — e.g. '384k' (YouTube), '192k' (social, the default). Omitted = the format's default (192k AAC). Lossless formats (wav, prores PCM) ignore it.

profile.description: Footage profile for the auto-run check battery (profile regression coverage): talking_head = the full strict battery (without an explicit profile, lufs applies only when normalize_loudness is set and silence_at_edges does not apply; an explicit profile turns both on, talking_head at -16 LUFS); silent_screen_demo waives lufs/caption_presence/silence_at_edges (recorded as waived_by_profile with the measured outcome kept) and runs a UI-tuned frozen-frame check. NOTE: the uniform_border check `uniform_border` is NOT waived by any profile — a baked-in margin is a defect on screen demos too. The receipt's footage_profile entry records the active profile + auto-detect proposal.

fit.description: Framing fit for sources whose aspect differs from the output frame. contain (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = letterbox/pillarbox (scale to fit inside, pad black, no pixels lost). cover = crop-to-fill (scale to cover the frame, centre-crop the overflow). Independent of the quality preset. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

resolution.description: Output geometry. project (DEFAULT, unchanged behavior) = the project settings width×height. match_source = the largest source video geometry on the timeline (a cropped clip contributes its crop rect; fps/audio_rate still come from project settings) — keeps high-res footage at native resolution instead of conforming down; a source larger than the frame limit (16 to 8192 px on each side, at most 8192x4320 pixels) is refused with invalid_args naming the limit. Omitting it replays byte-identical.

aspect.description: Reframe to this aspect for THIS render only (multi-format publish; project untouched): 9:16, 16:9, 1:1, 4:5, etc. Maps to 1080-baseline dims; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with resolution and width/height.

width.description: Explicit output width px (with height). The frame is 16 to 8192 px on each side and at most 8192x4320 pixels in total; odd values are rounded down to even. Overrides resolution; defaults fit to cover. Mutually exclusive with aspect/resolution.

height.description: Explicit output height px (with width; same frame limit as width).

normalize_loudness.description: Optional target integrated loudness in LUFS. Omitted = no normalization (byte-identical replay). When set, the lufs check also measures against this target, and single-pass ffmpeg loudnorm brings the mixed audio to this target (TP -1.5 dBTP before encoding, LRA 11); the encoded output must still meet -1 dBTP. Standard targets: -16 (long-form), -14 (social), -23 (EBU R128).

dry_run.description: When true, return the render PLAN (output geometry, realized duration, per-track manifest, the checks that will run) WITHOUT encoding — verify before a slow render. No job/op/file. The plan also carries `resources`: memory {estimate_mb, parts_mb {decode, encode, held_frames, overlays}, windows (a segmented render: its window count; the parts are its largest window's), encoder_threads, automatic_encoder_threads, adapted_encoder_threads, note, available_mb, limit_mb, total_mb, swap_mb, fits} and disk {estimate_mb, free_mb, volume, fits}, plus `refused` (the error a real render would get) and warnings[] memory_short / disk_short with the numbers and the way out. A real render runs the same check first: libx264 keeps its automatic thread count when the estimate fits the free memory (or SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_MEMORY_MB), else it uses the largest of 32/24/16/12/8/6/4 threads that fits (adapted_encoder_threads) and `note`, the job's progress message and the receipt's encode.memory_note say so; it is refused with out_of_memory when the estimate exceeds memory and swap together or with not_enough_space when even half the typical file does not fit, and otherwise starts with the same warnings on the envelope; its job result carries the same resources object. Sources larger than DCI 4K decode with 8 threads.

verbs.result: {job_id, render_id} — receipt arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks. A render that runs out of memory fails with code out_of_memory (the system stopped ffmpeg, or an allocation failed) and one whose output drive fills up fails with not_enough_space; both errors say what happened and what to do (free memory or space, keep the hardware encoder on, HEVC instead of H.264 at 8K, a lower resolution). A render whose ffmpeg writes no new output and uses under 2% of one processor core for 120 s (SHELLX_CUT_RENDER_STALL_SEC) is ended with code render_stalled: the message names the part of the timeline and the clip (clip_id, at_ms), the cause says whether it was held at its memory limit, the suggested_action what to change. A long reversed clip is rendered in windows whose reversed part fits the window memory budget.

result_schema.x-async-result: shellx-cut://receipts.schema.json#/$defs/RenderReceipt (arrives via receipt_ready / verify.checks; carries checks[] + fix_actions[] for the autopilot self-fix loop)
